name: English
titel: OrangeDeck: Bitcoin mempool visualizer, block height clock and Bitaxe monitor
beschreibung: Bitcoin mempool visualizer for Linux, Windows and Android, with a block height clock, Bitaxe monitor, block explorer and market data. Free and open source.
hero_text: Waiting transactions fall onto a heap as a tile mosaic, sized by what they move and coloured by age, fee or type. Confirmed ones fly into the block. You watch the network breathe.
was: OrangeDeck is a Bitcoin mempool visualizer. It draws the mempool the way it actually behaves: every waiting transaction is a square. It piles up, it gets mined, it gets replaced, and you see it happen instead of reading a number.

Around that sit five more views: a block height clock for a tablet on the wall, mining figures from your own Bitaxe and from the network, a block explorer, a market tab with candles, cumulative volume delta and liquidations, and watch-only addresses.
ansichten: The mempool as a living mosaic, with the last block beside it. Colour by age, fee or transaction type.
Block height, fees, price, hashrate and the halving countdown, large and without controls. For a tablet on the wall.
A Bitaxe monitor: hashrate, best share against the network difficulty, temperature and power of your own miner. Beside it the network with hashrate, difficulty and the next adjustment.
Search by height, hash, txid or address. Browse blocks and their contents, see what replaced what.
Price as candles or a line, volume, cumulative volume delta and liquidations, aggregated across exchanges.

Your own addresses or an xpub, watch-only. Your transactions are highlighted while they sit in the heap. Needs the OrangeDeck service on a Linux computer; phones and Windows reach it over the home network.
wo: An ordinary window. Wayland with an X11 fallback.
Layer-shell on niri, sway, Hyprland, river, labwc.
Listed in the DMS plugin directory. As a dashboard tab, a bar pill, a control center tile or a desktop widget.
A ZIP, unzip and run. The same views; the wallet comes from a service on a Linux computer in the same network.
Builds, but has not been tested yet. There is no package so far.
Phone or tablet. Each view has its own home screen shortcut.
warum: It is a viewer, and nothing else
It knows no private key, cannot sign, and carries no library that could. Watch-only means watch-only.
It talks to mempool.space or to your own node. There is no counting, no crash reports and no account.
Where a number is a model rather than a measurement, as with the liquidation heatmap, it says so on screen, with the assumptions written out.
The same QML draws the window, the widget, the panel and the phone. What is fixed in one place is fixed everywhere.
MIT licensed, no obfuscation, and the reasoning is in the commit messages rather than lost.
holen: Version {v}. ZIP for Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit: unzip and run orangedeck-app.exe. Not signed, SmartScreen asks on the first start.
Version {v}. Flatpak bundle: flatpak install --user orangedeck-{v}.flatpak. The runtime comes from Flathub.
From the DMS plugin directory: dms plugins install orangedeck. Runs on its own and uses the app's data when the app is running.
Version {v}. For Android 9 or newer, 64-bit ARM. Signed, the release notes give the fingerprint.
OrangeDeck's own repository. Add it once in F-Droid, Droid-ify or Neo Store, and updates arrive by themselves.
Takes every new version straight from the GitHub releases. Add the repository address as the source.
Release notes, checksums and older versions on GitHub.
faq: Does it need my keys?
No. It cannot sign anything. Watched addresses are entered as addresses or an xpub and never leave your machine except as a balance query.
Where does the data come from?
From mempool.space by default, or from your own mempool instance. That is a single setting. Market data comes from the exchanges' public feeds.
Does it phone home?
No. There is no server of ours, no analytics and no crash reporting.
What does it cost?
Nothing. It is MIT licensed and there is no paid tier.
Which languages does it speak?

Thirteen: English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese (Portugal and Brazil), Dutch, Russian, Japanese, Chinese, Polish and Czech. It starts in the system language, and numbers and dates follow the language you pick in the settings.
Is the liquidation heatmap real data?
No, and it says so on screen. Nobody publishes other people's positions; it is a model with its assumptions written out.
Can I run it on a tablet on the wall?
That is what the clock view is for: large figures, no controls. The Android build carries a shortcut straight into it.
fuss_herkunft: Tile packing and colour model ported from bitfeed (MIT, mononaut).

live.beispielHinweis: No stranger's miner and no stranger's wallet can be queried from here. These two views therefore show invented figures. The application shows yours.

seo_kurz: OrangeDeck is a free desktop and Android application that draws the Bitcoin mempool as a living tile mosaic. It combines six views in one window: mempool feed, block height clock, mining figures, block explorer, market data and watch-only addresses. It runs on Linux, Windows and Android and as a DankMaterialShell plugin, speaks thirteen languages, is MIT licensed and requires no account.
bilder: Clock: block height, fees, price and the next difficulty adjustment.
Mining: network hashrate and difficulty over one year.
Explorer: projected and confirmed blocks, the next block as tiles.
Market: candles and volume from Binance and Bybit.
quellen: The public WebSocket of mempool.space, or your own mempool instance. That is one setting.
The public streams of Binance, Bybit and OKX.
Bybit and OKX. The heatmap is a model built from Binance open interest, and it says so on screen.
The local API of the device, AxeOS or cgminer. The request stays in your home network.
Balance queries to the same mempool instance. No keys, and nothing else leaves the device.
alte_fassungen: Older versions, checksums and the full release notes are on GitHub.

unterseiten.name: Bitaxe monitor
unterseiten.karte: Hashrate, best share and temperature of your own miner, next to the network.
unterseiten.titel: Bitaxe monitor for Linux, Windows and Android | OrangeDeck
unterseiten.beschreibung: Watch your Bitaxe or any AxeOS or cgminer device: hashrate, best share against the network difficulty, temperature and power. Local, free, no account.
unterseiten.h1: A Bitaxe monitor next to the mempool
text: The Mining view of OrangeDeck reads your miner over its local API and shows hashrate, best share, temperature, power and fan speed. It detects AxeOS devices such as the Bitaxe and NerdAxe, and anything that speaks the cgminer API, for example Antminer, Avalon or Whatsminer.

The address is the only setting, and several miners go into the same field, separated by a vertical bar. The request goes to the device in your home network and nowhere else. There is no cloud account and no pool login.

The best share is held against the current network difficulty, and the view works out the chance of finding a block at your hashrate, per day and as an average interval. For a single Bitaxe that interval is very long, and OrangeDeck shows the number as it is.
Beside the device sits the network: hashrate and difficulty from 30 days back to 2009, the next difficulty adjustment, the average block time and the pool of the last block.
The view also runs as a widget: on Linux as a layer-shell surface on the desktop, on Windows as a frameless window, and on Android as a home screen widget.
unterseiten.bild_alt: The Mining view with network hashrate and difficulty over one year.
faq: Which miners does OrangeDeck support?
AxeOS devices such as the Bitaxe and NerdAxe, and miners with the cgminer API, for example Antminer, Avalon and Whatsminer.
Does the miner data leave my network?
No. OrangeDeck asks the device directly at its local address. Nothing goes through a server.
Can I watch several miners?
Yes. Enter the addresses in the settings, separated by a vertical bar, for example http://192.168.1.42|http://192.168.1.43.

unterseiten.name: Wall display
unterseiten.karte: Block height, fees and price in large figures, for an old tablet.
unterseiten.titel: Bitcoin block height display for a tablet on the wall | OrangeDeck
unterseiten.beschreibung: Turn an old Android tablet into a Bitcoin block height display: block height, fees, price, Moscow time and the halving countdown in large figures. Free, no account.
unterseiten.h1: A block height display for the wall
text: The Clock view shows the current block height in large figures, with fee, price, Moscow time, mempool size and hashrate below it. A bar counts down to the next difficulty adjustment, a line to the halving.
There are no controls on screen, so it reads well from across the room. What stands large in the middle can be changed in the settings, and if several values are chosen they take turns.

On Android the screen stays on while OrangeDeck runs in fullscreen. No permission is needed, and in the background the app keeps nothing awake. The Android build carries a home screen shortcut that opens the clock directly.
Any phone or tablet with Android 9 or newer and a 64-bit ARM processor will do. On a desktop the same view runs as a widget, for example in a corner of a second screen.
Price and Moscow time follow the currency you pick: euro, US dollar, pound, Swiss franc, Canadian or Australian dollar, or yen.
unterseiten.bild_alt: The Clock view with block height, fee, price, Moscow time, mempool and hashrate.
faq: Does the screen stay on?
Yes, on Android while the app is in fullscreen. When you leave fullscreen or switch apps, the normal screen timeout applies again.
Which tablets work?
Android 9 or newer with a 64-bit ARM processor. That covers most tablets from the last years.
Do I need my own node?
No. The numbers come from mempool.space. If you run your own mempool instance, enter its address and the clock uses that.

unterseiten.name: DankMaterialShell
unterseiten.karte: A bar pill, a control center tile and a desktop widget for DMS.
unterseiten.titel: Bitcoin dashboard plugin for DankMaterialShell | OrangeDeck
unterseiten.beschreibung: OrangeDeck as a DankMaterialShell plugin: mempool feed, block height clock, mining, explorer and market in a bar popout, plus a desktop widget. One command to install.
text: OrangeDeck is listed in the plugin directory of DankMaterialShell as OrangeDeck Bitcoin Dashboard. It installs with one command: dms plugins install orangedeck.

In the bar it sits as a pill with the number of waiting transactions. A click opens a popout with the same views as the app: Feed, Clock, Mining, Explorer and Market. There is also a control center tile and a desktop widget.

The plugin works without the app and fetches its data from mempool.space by itself. If the OrangeDeck app is installed and its service runs, the plugin uses that instead, so all windows share one connection.
It follows the language of DankMaterialShell and speaks the same thirteen languages as the app.
unterseiten.bild_alt: The OrangeDeck popout in the DankMaterialShell bar with the mempool feed.
faq: Which DMS version is needed?
DankMaterialShell 1.5.0 or newer, on any compositor that DMS supports.
Do I need the OrangeDeck app as well?
No. The plugin fetches everything itself. With the app and its service running, it shares their connection.
Where is the source?
In its own repository, github.com/orangedeck-dev/dms-plugin, generated from the main project. MIT licensed.
